mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the next 20 trading days signals accommodative monetary policy, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS declining by >1% over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% triggers increased consumer spending and business investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite UNRATE crossing below 5.0% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDP demand (GDPC1) and housing demand (HOUST) signal robust economic growth, amplifying corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 in a supply shock regime reduces corporate profit margins and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive despite INDPRO remaining below 95.0 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) coupled with increasing CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening cycle, raising borrowing costs and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a drop in GDP demand (GDPC1) below their 5-year averages indicates weakening growth, reducing corporate investment and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive despite both GDPC1 and INDPRO falling below their averages.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) coupled with falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) indicates a labor market recovery and accommodative policy, boosting consumer confidence and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market expansion with easing policy
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and FEDFUNDS move in the predicted directions.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 5% in a late-cycle expansion regime signals peak demand, driving up corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite GDPC1 exceeding the previous quarter's value.
